extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners before the USPTO; OED/USPTO disciplinary staff; attorneys facing reciprocal discipline
extracted.subtask_description: Final Order under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 imposing exclusion from practice before the USPTO based on state disbarment; explains service, notice and response procedures, statutory/regulatory basis, specific misconduct findings, and post-exclusion duties and prohibitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for reciprocal discipline under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 / 11.804(h)
rubrics_metrics.description: Exclusion ordered for violation of 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h), predicated upon being disbarred on ethical grounds from the practice of law by a duly constituted authority of a State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This action is taken pursuant to the provisions of 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.24. The Notice of Exclusion states the respondent was disbarred by the Supreme Court of the State of New Hampshire on ethical grounds, and that exclusion from practice before the USPTO is appropriate for such a predicate state disciplinary decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific misconduct supporting state disbarment
rubrics_metrics.description: The state court found respondent violated New Hampshire's Rules of Professional Conduct 1.1, 1.3, 1.4, 1.15, 3.3, 8.1(b), 8.4(c), and 8.4(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically, the conduct included: misappropriating funds from a special needs trust; failing to account for client funds in his possession; filing false trust accounting certificates; and failing to respond to the New Hampshire Attorney Discipline Office's lawful demand for information. These factual findings supplied the predicate for reciprocal discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service requirements for Notice and Order (37 C.F.R. §§ 11.24 and 11.35)
rubrics_metrics.description: Notice and Order must be served on respondent in accordance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.35.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice and Order was mailed by certified mail to the address of record. 37 C.F.R. § 11.35(a)(2) permits service on a registered practitioner by Priority Mail Express®, first-class mail, or any delivery service that provides the ability to confirm delivery or attempted delivery to the address provided to OED pursuant to § 11.11. Forwarding of mail and delivery to a different address (with confirmed delivery) can satisfy service requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to notify OED of address and address changes (37 C.F.R. § 11.11(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: A registered practitioner is obligated to notify the OED Director of his postal address for his office and every change to any of said addresses within thirty days of the date of the change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the practitioner fails to update the address of record, any fault in not receiving mailed Notices lies with the practitioner; service sent to the address of record remains proper. The Order notes the Respondent did not appear to satisfy this obligation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity to respond and time for filing a response
rubrics_metrics.description: The Notice and Order provides the respondent an opportunity to file, within forty (40) days, a response opposing the imposition of reciprocal discipline identical to that imposed by the state, based on one or more of the reasons provided in 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice must inform the respondent of the 40-day filing period and the statutory grounds for opposing reciprocal discipline (as enumerated in § 11.24(d)(1)); absence of such a response is consequential (see next entry).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequence of failure to respond (no genuine issue of material fact)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the respondent fails to file a response to the Notice and Order, there is no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d) and exclusion from practice is appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order determined, in light of Respondent's failure to file a response, that reciprocal exclusion from practice of patent, trademark and other non-patent law before the USPTO is the appropriate discipline. This establishes the procedural consequence for non-response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and notice of discipline (37 C.F.R. § 11.59)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish a Notice in the Official Gazette and give notice pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.59 of the public discipline and the reasons for the discipline to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the states of admission, to courts where respondent is known to be admitted, and to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order includes the specific Notice of Exclusion text to be published and indicates that disciplinary decisions are available for public review at the OED FOIA Reading Room (URL provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: Duties of excluded practitioner (37 C.F.R. § 11.58)
rubrics_metrics.description: An excluded practitioner must comply with the duties enumerated in 37 C.F.R. § 11.58.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order directs Respondent to comply with § 11.58; while the Order does not restate § 11.58's text, it signals required post-discipline obligations (e.g., notice to clients, transfer of files, and other duties set forth in that regulation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissociation from USPTO Customer Numbers and PKI certificates; prohibitions on obtaining Customer Numbers
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO will dissociate respondent's name from any Customer Numbers and the public key infrastructure (PKI) certificate associated with those Customer Numbers; respondent shall not apply for or obtain a USPTO Customer Number, nor have his name added to a USPTO Customer Number, unless and until reinstated to practice before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an affirmative operational consequence of exclusion: loss of ability to use Customer Numbers/PKI and a bar on obtaining or associating with them until reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory and regulatory authority for imposing discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: Disciplinary action is taken pursuant to 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.24.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order cites these provisions as the legal basis for reciprocal discipline; practitioners and OED staff should rely on these authorities when initiating or responding to reciprocal discipline proceedings.
